solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to leave is to part

explanation.surface: Someone sets off up a hill riding in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going uphill' turns PART into TRAP; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, a kind of carriage.

parts.note: a mass is a large group or crowd

indicators.note: a race that is fixed is rigged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a big field of runners was beaten because the race was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges RACE into ACRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre an opponent is informal for beating them overwhelmingly, the same as trouncing.

clue.text: Legendary princess died in one, alone

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: died is set within the pair of words that follow, one and alone

parts.note: sole means alone or only

explanation.surface: A princess of legend died in solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside ISOLE, made of I and SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Sly type having row about stray dog

parts.note: a fox is proverbially a sly, cunning creature

indicators.note: row goes round stray, wrapping it about

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray

explanation.surface: A cunning character with a row of something around a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the row word round the stray word to make the dog's second word; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox terrier is a breed of small dog originally used to flush foxes.

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Sacking a colleague who has a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is an example of a firearm, which the 'say' signals.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
rump is a cut of steak

explanation.surface: A dowdy woman serves up a good steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a dowdy, unfashionably dressed woman.

clue.text: What one may do with 17 is spend more time than is necessary

definitions.meaning: 17 across is the leftover-dinner name of a dish, and a cold bird could literally be made into a meal

definitions.text: spend more time than is necessary
definitions.meaning: to make a big production out of a simple task, taking too long over it

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is COLD TURKEY, read literally as cold roast turkey meat, which one could serve as a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make unnecessarily heavy work of something, taking more time and fuss than needed.

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Someone haughtily turns down a second bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn something is to reject it with contempt, refusing it disdainfully.

indicators.note: bombed means blown apart, so the letters of the porcelain town are scattered

explanation.surface: Meissen, the German porcelain town, was bombed in wartime revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, named after the Greek goddess of vengeance, means deserved punishment or retribution.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by strange tailless cat

parts.note: rum is British informal for strange or odd

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word for a cat is cut off

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A commotion is set off by an odd cat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the last S of PUSS to leave PUS; 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or disturbance.

clue.text: Take out US mag to do something whilst waiting

parts.note: to take out someone is slang for killing them
Time is a well-known American news magazine

explanation.surface: Someone takes a US magazine out to read in a waiting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'Take out' looks like borrowing the magazine but means murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to occupy oneself with something while waiting for time to pass.

definitions.meaning: to value or feel thankful for something
to increase in value, as property or shares do

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to be thankful for something and to gain in value over time.

clue.text: Man, the artist Prince, US rhythm and blues singer

parts.note: Man Ray was an American surrealist artist and photographer
Charles was long the Prince of Wales

explanation.surface: A list naming a man, an artist, a royal and an American soul singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a generic person, but with 'the artist' it is Man Ray; Prince Charles is himself known as a watercolour painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Charles was a celebrated American singer and pianist, a pioneer of rhythm and blues and soul.

indicators.note: the opening letter of the driver's title is removed, chauffeur beginning with C

parts.note: a crash is a collision

explanation.surface: A careless crash happens, though not the chauffeur's first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not chauffeur's first' removes C from CRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without considering the consequences, synonymous with reckless.

clue.text: Currant buns? I feel my secret is out

indicators.note: a secret that is out has been let loose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they feel their secret has been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly cemeteries is British slang for currant-filled pastries, the squashed currants looking like dead flies; the question mark flags the jokey name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British slang name for currant slices or buns, the dark fruit resembling dead insects.

indicators.note: rush is set into appropriate, placed within it

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable
to leap is to rush or spring forward

explanation.surface: Someone rushes into a suitable movie house.
explanation.walkthrough: A fleapit is a British slang term for a shabby old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleapit is informal British for a run-down, grubby cinema.

clue.text: Ten fancy cake topping — it's tempting

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: icing is the sugary topping on a cake

explanation.surface: Ten fancy cakes with icing look tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing means attractive and alluring, the same as tempting.

indicators.note: the hyphenated word holds the run of letters concealed inside it

explanation.surface: A timeshare arrangement conceals a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net, the kind of network used to trap creatures.

clue.text: Method of treating drug addiction in distant country

parts.note: cold means distant or aloof in manner
Turkey is a country

explanation.surface: A rehab method is practised in a faraway land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the abrupt withdrawal of an addictive drug without tapering off, a recognised way of breaking addiction.

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A tax licence for selling meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excise' reads as the duty but is the verb meaning remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a small piece of meat, as a chop from the neck of lamb.

clue.text: Level before start of throwing competition

indicators.note: the word for level comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: even means level or flat

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word throwing is taken

explanation.surface: Things are level just before the throwing contest starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest within a sports meeting, a competition.

clue.text: Preprandial drink provided by a retiring salesman, Italian

indicators.note: provided is placed beside the rest, at the end
retiring means going back, so the salesman word is read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it
provided that means on condition that, the same as if

explanation.surface: A drink before dinner is offered by a salesman from Italy who is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses the salesman word; 'by' means beside, so the condition word goes after the Italian piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

indicators.note: miss is absorbed into court, taken inside it

parts.note: to lose something is to miss it, as a chance

explanation.surface: A young woman is absorbed in a secret of the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman's title but is the verb; 'engrossed by' wraps the court abbreviation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means secret or hidden, as in a closet admirer.

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter of the port is removed

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Wine from an unopened bottle of port has settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is England's main ferry port facing France; 'unopened' drops its D. 'Port' looks like the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means finished or concluded, as a matter that has been settled.

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The topic of a newspaper article is the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them, tan their hide
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Beating a man is said to be moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like moving but is the geometric sense of meeting at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, tangent means touching a curve at a single point without crossing it.
